newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA STUDIES WAYS TO FUND WATER PROJECTS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA STUDIES WAYS TO FUND WATER PROJECTS.

text.p: Water Affairs and Forestry Minister Kader Asmal said on Tuesday he had asked four businessmen to advise him on the creation of a utility to fund water projects.
He told a parliamentary briefing his department could not borrow funds for capital projects but had a very limited budget despite South Africa's huge water needs.
His department had prepared a scheme for seven or eight major capital projects but had a budget of only 200 million rand, "which is derisory".
The smallest scheme would alone cost 300 million rand.
"So what I am initiating is a process where we consider different options as to what kind of parastatal utility with capacity to borrow money that we can set up," Asmal said.
"We want to set up sustainable projects that pay for themselves, like the Lesotho Highlands scheme."

The businessmen who had been contacted for advice were Development Bank of Southern Africa chief executive Ian Goldin, Thebe Investments chief executive Vusi Khanyile, Industrial Development Corporation deputy managing director Jan de Bruyn and TransCaledon Tunnel Authority chairman Trevor Fowler.
